reason: planning stopped before any code was written: the plan still needed revising in the last round (round 3 of 3). I read drain.rs (Drain::land, attempts, the Steps and Lander traits), the Athena::land_pr wrapper in gh/landing.rs, close.rs and athena-git. The functions the plan names exist where it says: landed_commit_for, land_pr, after_merge, resync_tip and resync_onto_merge, Git::replay, merge_tree, reset_keep and fetch_remote_branch. plan_rebase is new code; the reading listed it as though it already existed. The queue design follows from the code. The slot belongs to the item and lasts through the landing retry, matching the two land calls at drain.rs:1428-1437. A conflict ends the item without a retry and without a stop. Criteria 1 to 5 each have a deterministic demonstration that uses production plan_rebase, rebased_from and Drain::land. The threaded test is honestly labelled a smoke test. The one soundness problem is the left-behind rule. When a later job rebases, the held-back job's landing commit leaves the local branch. That commit carries the job's closing records (close.rs:1-7), and Records::load reads job state from that branch (landing.rs:429-431). So the rule quietly does the record-dropping drop_landed that the reading put in A6b, and that decision 1 rejects for that very reason. That is a major finding, so the verdict is revise. Carry the conflicting commit's records without its code, or get a ruling from the user. Smaller points: carrying clean unlanded commits weakens the NeedsRecheck guarantee the CHANGELOG would state; queue order is pass order, not stacking order; and the plan should name a cut line for size. I weighed Athena's gh/mod.rs finding; that one-line re-export is needed and is disclosed, so I did not repeat it. Findings: minor: crates/athena-core/src/gh/mod.rs is not among the reading's deliverables (files, crates/athena-core/src/gh/mod.rs); major: The left-behind rule removes a held-back job's records. This is the deferred drop_landed under another name, and the plan's own rejected option ruled it out. (Plan decision 1 (left-behind rule) and the first open question; crates/athena-core/src/run/close.rs:1-7, 210; crates/athena-core/src/gh/landing.rs:429-431); minor: `plan_rebase` carries every earlier unlanded commit that replays cleanly. Content from a job that is Blocked or NeedsRecheck therefore reaches main inside the next job's pull request, which contradicts the guarantee the CHANGELOG will state. (Plan decision 1 ('a clean b would push unlanded content') vs the plan_rebase algorithm; criterion 7 CHANGELOG text on NeedsRecheck); minor: Queue order is the order jobs join, which can differ from the order their landing commits were stacked. The head job could then carry another unlanded job's commit that sits below it. (Decision 3 (queue join at RunStep::Passed) vs land_or_block stacking order); minor: The plan is large for one producer run: about 20 new tests across two crates, a stack-aware replay, bare-origin flows and an Athena wrapper fixture. The earlier job failed partly on size. (Plan as a whole: Files, Steps 2-8, the Demonstrations)
